newsitem.title: CHINA: China tightens rules on explosives.
newsitem.headline: China tightens rules on explosives.

text.p: Chinese police have seized tonnes of gunpowder and uncovered thousands of safety breaches in a new crackdown on the misuse of explosives, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Explosives for civilian use are widely available in China, which regularly suffers lethal blasts caused by careless owners, illicit fireworks producers, disgruntled former employees and jilted lovers.

Chinese police investigated 132,000 companies involved in the production or use of explosives and withdrew 881 licences after uncovering 65,000 breaches of safety regulations between March and June, Xinhua said.
In the eastern province of Shandong, police seized 36 tonnes of gunpowder and 96,000 detonators and closed several illegal explosives factories, sales outlets and stores, it said.
The number of gunpowder accidents between March and June plummeted 40.5 percent and the number of blast cases fell 9.7 percent compared with the same period last year, it said.
The crackdown was announced on the same day Chinese officials revealed that a woman in the southern province of Guangdong had killed herself, her lover and five others with a pack of dynamite.
The woman had argued with her married lover, prompting her to detonate the bomb and almost totally destroyed the three-storey building where they were staying, said one local official.
